key_insight: ScienceIDE turns scientific code repositories into learnable, programmable environments for AI agents, making decades of scientific software usable as training ground and testbed. It tackles the gap between executable scientific code and the domain knowledge needed for reliable agent learning.
problem_solved: Scientific code is abundant but hard for AI agents to learn from because it is fragmented across toolchains, full of implicit domain conventions, and judged by specialized correctness criteria. This creates a "scientific experience bottleneck" that prevents reliable agent training and evaluation.
method: Builds infrastructure that converts scientific code into programmable environments for agents.
Uses expert-defined scientific guidance to encode domain-specific rules, conventions, and correctness signals.
Creates an interaction layer that lets agents learn by operating on real scientific repositories rather than isolated toy tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ScienceIDE offers a path to train and benchmark agents on realistic scientific workflows instead of simplified synthetic tasks. This could improve agent reliability, domain transfer, and usefulness in research-heavy settings.
